summary: Axer Space Run is a free browser-based educational game that turns spacecraft mission design into hands-on play. Players choose a solar-system target, then balance rocket capacity, power (solar or nuclear), antennas, instruments, orbit, and budget. Every choice affects mass, data return, and fail risk—from about 1% on solid designs up to roughly 50% when a mission is overweight, underpowered, or too risky. Failures are explained in plain language so players learn why a mission broke.During the cruise, they walk the ship, view planet facts, play trivia, and try a short runner minigame before scores, ranks, and badges arrive. The whole experience is a single HTML file—no install—so it works on classroom computers and phones.By making real engineering tradeoffs visible and replayable, the game helps students build intuition for how exploration missions are planned, why constraints matter, and how science is returned from other worlds.
details:
Axer Space Run is a free browser game that teaches real rocket design through play. Players plan missions across the solar system—from the Moon to Europa—by choosing rockets, power systems, antennas, and science instruments while staying inside mass, power, data, and budget limits.

This was developed by Sajeed Hasan and some use of AI

Every choice has consequences. An overweight craft can fail at launch. Too little power or a weak antenna can cut the science return. Fail risk rises from about 1% on solid designs toward 50% when the mission is stressed. During the cruise, players walk the ship, look outside at planet facts, run trivia, and play a short runner minigame before scores, ranks, and badges come in.

This game can be downloaded as a single html file—no install—so it works in classrooms and at home. It turns abstract mission-design tradeoffs into something students can try, fail, fix, and try again, building intuition for how real exploration missions are planned.
